title: feat(cli): os migrate option-codes rewrites option values still stored as a number, a boolean or SQLite "N.0" text to the code string (#29643)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-warren"} -->
_Requested by **Warren** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8?thread=cmsg_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8VQJupmprD1XpcbZZYuS4Kh)_
Fixes #29643

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:新增 `os migrate option-codes`,把 #29562 之前写进选项字段的旧值(内存驱动的原始数字/布尔、SQLite 的 `"3.0"`/`"1.0"`/`"0.0"`、多值数组里的原始元素)一次性改写成写入口如今存的选项码字符串。
- 为什么改:旧行与新行存成两种形态,`{ f: "3" }` 筛不到旧行、读出来是旧形态、唯一字段上新 `"3"` 与旧 `"3.0"` 不冲突(#29643 实测)。
- 风险与回滚:默认只读演练;`--apply` 只改能判定的值,判不了的(无选项字段上的 `"3.0"`、`"1"` 与 `"true"` 同时声明时的 `"1.0"`、读成未声明码的值)只列出不改;回滚即撤 PR,已改写的值与新写入同形。
- 先看:① `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/option-codes.ts` 的 `decideOptionCode`(判定表);② 同文件 `migrateOptionCodes` 的整行改写与逐行失败;③ `option-codes.integration.test.ts`(真实 SQLite)。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project integration src/commands/migrate/option-codes.integration.test.ts`,应见 26/26 通过。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

- **New command `os migrate option-codes`** (`packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/option-codes.ts`), the data half of #29562: a sibling of `os migrate blank-single-values`, not an arm of `os migrate value-shapes`. `value-shapes` documents that it rewrites nothing, and the server seat's ruling on #29431 (record 6588116815) put the last rewriting step beside it rather than in it, so this one follows that precedent. It walks every option-family field (`SINGLE_OPTION_TYPES` ∪ `MULTI_OPTION_TYPES` from `@objectstack/spec/data`, the sets the #29562 door reads; a `multiple: true` select or radio is walked as an array), `readonly` ones included, by keyset on `id`.
- **The decision (`decideOptionCode`)**, per stored scalar or per array element:
  - a raw number or boolean is decidable by type and becomes `String(value)`; on a field declaring codes, only when that string is one, else it is reported `undeclared`;
  - a SQLite `"N.0"` that is not itself a declared code is decidable only against the declared codes: its readings are `String(Number(s))`, plus `"true"` for `"1.0"` and `"false"` for `"0.0"`; exactly one declared reading → that code, none → `undeclared`, two → `ambiguous`, no declared codes → `free-field`;
  - a picklist-bound field whose options did not resolve is reported `picklist-unresolved`;
  - every other string and `null` is left alone.
  
  A multi-value array is rewritten whole only when every old element in it is decidable, so no row ends half-migrated.
- **Dry run by default**, as the family does: counts per object and field, a few `stored → code` samples, no row written, read-only boot. `--apply` writes each affected row once through the engine in the system context; a failure (a unique collision with a row that already holds the code) is a per-row failure and the walk goes on. `--object` narrows and refuses an undeclared name; `--apply` keeps the SQLite occupancy gate (`--force`); `--json` keeps stdout parseable. No deployment flag: a re-run that reports nothing to rewrite is the verification.
- **Rosters**: the new command joins the three family pins its sibling sits in (`schema-migrate.one-shot-family.integration.test.ts`, `migrate-confirmation-exit.pin.test.ts`, `json-stdout-purity.e2e.test.ts`) and gets a row and a section in `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`.
- **Changeset** `.changeset/29643-migrate-option-codes.md`: `@objectstack/cli` patch, both declaration lines.
- No `packages/spec/**` hunk, no write-door change, no `protocol.ts`, no new error code.

## Why

Wanted 1 asked to measure first. Rows written below the engine's door (what the pre-#29562 door handed the driver; PR #29638's recording-driver pin shows it passed the raw scalar through), then a fresh engine on the same store, at `origin/main` `7dae3b3c`:

| question | SQLite (`SqlDriver`, file) | driver-memory (`persistence: 'file'`) |
|:--|:--|:--|
| stored `3` / `true` / `false` on a single select | `"3.0"` / `"1.0"` / `"0.0"` | `3` / `true` / `false` |
| stored `[3, true]` on a multiselect | JSON `[3,true]` | `[3, true]` |
| engine read | the old form as stored | the old form as stored |
| `{ coded: "3" }`, `{ coded: "true" }`, `{ free: "3" }` | no row | no row |
| `{ free: 3 }` | the `"3.0"` row | the `3` row |
| `{ multi: { $contains: "3" } }` | the `[3,true]` row | the `[3,true]` row |
| unique `uq`: insert `"3"` beside an old `3` / `"3.0"` | admitted beside it | admitted beside it |
| unique `uq`: then insert `3` | 409 (collides with the new `"3"`) | 409 |
| text field `42` (#29241, item 3) | `"42.0"` | `42` |

So one option splits into two stored values on both drivers, which is what this rewrite closes. A raw scalar is decidable by its type; a SQLite `"N.0"` is decidable only when the field declares exactly one of its readings, which is why the free-field case is reported and never rewritten.

**Item 3, the text family (#29241): not folded in; its own card is named in the report.** Its decidable part is only driver-memory's raw `42` / `true`: on SQLite a text field holds `"42.0"`, and with no declared codes nothing can tell an old `42` from text someone typed, so a text pass could rewrite nothing on SQLite and would have to stay silent there. The text family's set (`BOUNDED_STRING_FIELD_TYPES`) also takes in `password`, whose reads a walk would have to treat differently. That makes it a different decision from this one, so it gets its own card rather than an arm here.

## Acceptance notes

1. **driver-memory is measured, not a test backend.** The walk test runs on SQLite only: a first version also ran on `InMemoryDriver` and `check:driver-memory-census` refused the new consumer (exit 1, `x LEDGERED: … option-codes.integration.test.ts:26`). The ruling there is the maintainer's, so the consumer was dropped rather than ledgered. driver-memory's face (a raw scalar on a single-value field) is the `scalar` arm of `decideOptionCode`, pinned by the decision table, and the same arm runs end to end on SQLite through the raw JSON elements of `multi` / `tags`.
2. **Postgres / MySQL: NOT MEASURED** (no server in this container). A JS number bound into a `text` column there is sent as its decimal string, so the `"N.0"` arm is not expected to fire; the raw-element arm in JSON arrays applies on every driver.
3. **Filter face, observed and not changed**: on base, `{ free: 3 }` (a number comparand) matches an old SQLite `"3.0"` row through SQLite's own numeric comparison, and the old raw `3` on driver-memory. How a number comparand should read against option codes belongs to #29486; this PR does not touch the filter door.
